lessons.title: 1.6 SOUNDS
topics: INTRODUCTION:
This topic introduces learners to the world of sounds through listening, identifying, and creating
them. Sounds are part of our everyday life, and they can be natural (like birds singing or wind
blowing) or artificial (like car horns or bells). Learners will explore and experiment with different
sources of sound to develop listening, creativity, and expression skills.
activities: Task 1 – Sound Scavenger Hunt

lessons.title: 1.9 ICT DEVICES IN EVERYDAY LIFE
topics: INTRODUCTION
In this topic, learners will be introduced to basic ICT devices that they encounter in real life sit-
uations. They will learn to identify, use, and handle devices such as desktop computers, laptops,
smart phones, televisions, and radios. This topic helps learners develop familiarity with technology,
enhances their curiosity, and builds foundational digital literacy skills.
activities: Toy phones, keyboards, or other ICT tools.
Educational videos on ICT devices.
Storybooks or posters related to ICT devices.
Learners to explore real ICT devices or picture of ICT devices such as (a desktop, lap-
top, smart phone, television, radio, printer
Task 2: Marching ICT Devices with their names
Learners to match ICT devices with their correct names. (If possible, use toy versions or
real objects for hands-on learning).
assessment: Assess the ability to identify and name different ICT devices (desktop, laptop,
smartphone, television, printer
Assess the ability to operate ICT devices, specifically turning them on and off correctly.
Assess the ability to apply their understanding of ICT devices to complete tasks, such as
switching devices on/off and simulating digital communication scenarios.
ICT devices are fun and helpful tools that can make learning and communication more exciting.

lessons.title: 1.10 COMPUTER SOFTWARE
topics: INTRODUCTION
In this topic, learners will be introduced to basic computer software concepts through interactive
educational games. They will explore how games can be used as learning tools to enhance problem-
solving, creativity, and digital literacy. By engaging with computer educational games, learners
will develop hand-eye coordination, critical thinking, and decision-making skills.
activities: Task 1: Demonstrate how to play
− Let learners try simple actions like clicking or tapping to interact to interact with
computer games.
Task 2: Let Learners explore the games
− Learners to explore different educational games.
Teacher to give the following important reminders for playing games:
− Follow Instructions – Listen to what the game says and do what it asks.
− Use the Mouse, Keyboard, or Touch screen gently – click, drag, or tap carefully.
assessment: Assess ability to interact with computer games by performing basic actions like clicking,
tapping, or using a mouse or touchscreen.
Assess ability to follow game instructions, listening carefully and performing tasks as
directed by the game.
Assess collaborative behaviour by sharing the computer or tablet with peers and taking
turns during game time.
